storm.summary_layperson: No storms are showing up on radar or in the models for Riverside this evening — expect a quiet, mostly clear evening with just light wind.
storm.local_effect_blurb: No storm is in the picture tonight, so the marine layer isn't being tested — and what little is there is thin anyway, a 5°F air-water gap now that's already fading to near zero by around 7 PM.
storm.detail_html:
Radar (KOKX) shows no storm cells within range of Riverside this evening, and today's HRRR run puts CAPE at 0 J/kg — there's essentially no instability to work with. The latest Area Forecast Discussion from OKX agrees: while 0-6km shear is a healthy 38-40 kt, the office notes instability is limited, yielding "a very low BRN," and that severe weather "looks unlikely at this point." No watches or warnings are in effect.

The one thunderstorm mention in today's AFD is for Thursday afternoon and evening, not tonight — a separate, later system outside this window.

Because there's no storm approaching, the Sound's usual protective marine-layer effect isn't being tested tonight. For the record, that layer is thin regardless: the air-water gap is 5°F now, and trend data shows it fading to under 1°F by around 7 PM as the air cools toward evening — so even if something did try to develop later, there'd be little buffer left to lean on.

Bottom line for the cove and surrounding towns alike: a calm, mostly sunny evening with no meaningful storm risk. The call would change only if a fresh line of convection appears on radar upstream, which nothing in the current data suggests.

wind.tactics_blurb: Very light gradient wind with no sea breeze in play — expect a shifty, drifting evening in the cove; favor the middle of the course and play each puff as it comes.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
This is a gradient-wind day, not a sea-breeze day. The air-water temperature difference is right at the usual thermal gate (5°F), but none of the coastal or inland stations are showing the southerly wind component a sea breeze needs — 0% of stations, coastal or inland, are reading southerly. Without that ingredient, the sea-breeze maturation correction doesn't apply, and the wind table below uses the raw model direction.

The synoptic gradient itself is barely there: the authoritative airport-anemometer average is just 5.2 kt, well under the 8 kt line for even a "moderate" gradient day — this is a light gradient (no sea breeze) evening.

⚠️ Model/observation divergence: HRRR forecasts the wind swinging E–ESE at 2-4 kt through the window, but Riverside YC and most nearby stations are currently reading NNW/WNW instead (roughly a 90° gap). At these wind speeds, direction is inherently noisy and low-confidence in both the model and the obs — treat the forecast direction for this window as a rough guide, not a precise call. Expect puffs to wander, possibly including offshore-feeling breeze off the NW shore rather than the modeled easterly flow.

HRRR data only extends to 7:00 PM this cycle; the 8, 9, and 10 PM rows are extrapolated from the trend, not sourced from a fresh forecast hour.

Favored side: center. With no organized driver and readings this light, pressure will be patchy rather than lined up on one shore — the middle of the course is the safest bet to avoid getting parked in a hole near either shoreline. Expect drifting conditions: mostly 1-4 kt with occasional puffs to 6-8 kt, better suited to light-air specialists than a normal breeze-on evening.
